data.title: Provincial Nominee Program (PNP)
data.subtitle: Immigrate to Canada through the province that values your skills most.
data.intro_title: Build Your Future in a Province That Needs You
data.intro_description: The Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) offers a unique opportunity for individuals with the right skills, experience, and education to become permanent residents of Canada—through targeted streams chosen by each province. Whether you're applying directly or through Express Entry, Velox Immigration will guide you through the right PNP path, from nomination to PR.

data.what_we_offer_intro: We help you choose and navigate the right PNP stream based on your education, occupation, work experience, and ties to a province:

what_we_offer_items.title: Skilled Worker Streams (Direct or Express Entry-linked)
what_we_offer_items.description: Each province and territory has unique criteria based on local labour needs. We assess which stream best suits your background and help you prepare your Expression of Interest (EOI) or provincial application—whether through British Columbia, Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, or others.

what_we_offer_items.title: Employer-Sponsored or Job Offer Streams
what_we_offer_items.description: Some PNPs require a job offer from a provincial employer. We work closely with both the applicant and the employer to prepare the employer forms, compliance letters, and offer documentation.

what_we_offer_items.title: International Graduate Streams
what_we_offer_items.description: Graduates of eligible institutions in provinces like Ontario, Nova Scotia, and Manitoba may qualify for PR through tailored PNP streams. We support you in transitioning from study or work permit to PR status.

what_we_offer_items.title: PNP-Aligned Express Entry Profiles
what_we_offer_items.description: We also help eligible candidates in the Express Entry pool receive 600 bonus CRS points through a provincial nomination, drastically increasing the chance of receiving an ITA.

data.what_you_need_to_apply:
While requirements vary by province and stream, applicants generally need:

  • A valid passport
  • A clear and detailed resume or CV
  • Language test results (IELTS/CELPIP/TEF)
  • Proof of education (transcripts, ECA if foreign credentials)
  • Proof of work experience
  • Job offer letter (if applicable)
  • Connection to the province (education, work, relatives, or prior stay)
  • Settlement funds (varies by stream)

Each province has its own documentation and submission portal—we manage all of this for you.

faq_items.question: Do I need a job offer to apply for PNP?
faq_items.answer: Not always. Some streams are open to individuals with work or study experience in the province, or strong credentials alone.

faq_items.question: Can I apply to multiple provinces at once?
faq_items.answer: You can't apply to more than one province at the same time if you're in an active process. But we can assess which one offers the strongest chance.

faq_items.question: What's the difference between PNP and Express Entry?
faq_items.answer: PNP is run by provinces; Express Entry is federal. Some PNP streams are aligned with Express Entry and offer bonus points.

faq_items.question: Do I need to live in the province after nomination?
faq_items.answer: Yes—at least initially. Each nomination is based on the genuine intention to settle in that province.

faq_items.question: Is there a fee to apply for PNP?
faq_items.answer: Yes, most provinces charge a processing fee. We'll advise you on costs depending on the province you apply to.

faq_items.question: What is the processing time?
faq_items.answer: Times are estimates and vary by province and stream. See individual PNP portals for updates.
